title: `AudioStreamInteractive`'s `RETURN_TO_HOLD` / `hold_previous` does not work if last played clip is holding previous
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.dev5.official [a8643700c]
- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev5 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Radeon RX 580 Series (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21923.1000) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9600KF CPU @ 3.70GHz (6 threads) - 15.91 GiB memory (using WASAPI)

### Issue description

I have an `AudioStreamPlayer` with `AudioStreamInteractive` as a resource. I'm trying to return to the first clip, after the second clip finishes, using the `hold_previous` functionality. But at the end of the second clip, nothing happens.

I've spent hours on this, including poking around the source code. I feel like me setup isn't wrong, but I also find it a bit hard to believe this bug, if it exists, hasn't been reported yet, so I'm hoping I misunderstood something and I'm doing something wrong.

Working on this because I'm rewriting parts of the docs for AudioStreams for a future PR, and I'm trying to understand this audio stream resource so I can properly document it. But these two properties have been very confusing.

Issue is not project dependent, but including an MRP anyway. The script has helpful info. I recomment running the scene instead of just playing the stream from the editor.

I intend on trying to fix this myself, but I just needed to confirm this is an actual bug.

**EDIT:** I think I figured out what is going on. What doesn't work is the return to hold functionality when there are only two clips to transition back and forth. The second clip can't return to the first using this functionality. Or I guess in more general terms, return to hold doesn't work if the last clip played is the one holding previous.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create an audio player node
- Set `stream` to `AudioStreamInteractive`
- Add two clips
- Set clip `0` to auto-advance to clip `1`
- Set clip `1`'s auto-advance to `Return To Hold`
- In `Edit Transitions`, enable transition from clip `0` to clip `1` (this works via code too)
- In that transition, set `Hold Previous` to `true`
- Play the stream

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[audio-stream-interactive-return-to-hold-mrp-(public).zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27166065/audio-stream-interactive-return-to-hold-mrp-.public.zip)
